To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transcription‐associated mutation generates de novo splice sites and alternative splice isoforms in highly expressed genes, which is a major new source of selectable variation.

the most highly expressed genes in the genome, hemoglobin genes in the falcon genome, produce a large number of transcript isoforms, which are mainly generated by de novo splice site mutations, and that the mutation rate is higher in these highly expressed genes than expected from the mutation rate in other parts of the genome, suggesting a new mechanism for generating RNA complexity in the genome.
transcription‐associated mutation is a major source of RNA complexity, and this mechanism can promote gene expression diversity and enhance organismal fitness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the origin of RNA diversity, the mechanism of TAM, and the physiological significance of TAM‐associated RNA complexity.
the origin of transcript diversity, and its biological function.
the mechanism generating the diversity of spliced transcripts, which is the basis for the diversity of proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transcription‐associated mutation mechanism, not RNA editing, is a major source of alternative splicing and isoform diversity in highly expressed genes and that it may be a major source of selectable variation in the evolution of organisms.
TAM‐induced alternative splicing is a major new mechanism for generating RNA complexity in highly expressed genes, providing a new source of selectable variation.
transcription‐associated mutation is a new source of selectable variation that can generate RNA complexity in highly expressed genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the high‐expressed genes in falcon blood are prone to generate alternative isoforms by TAM, and these isoforms may be important in their survival on the Qinghai‐Tian Plateau, where oxygen levels are low.
transcription-associated mutation (TAM) promotes RNA complexity in highly expressed genes, which is a major new source of selectable variation.
TAM is a major source of selectable genetic variation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the high expression of a gene is associated with the generation of more transcript isoforms by transcription‐associated mutations (TAM).
transcription‐associated mutation, a previously unappreciated process, may be a major source of selectable genetic variation.
the enormous diversity of transcript isoforms is not a random process but a consequence of transcriptional activity.
